name: Rusty6502
description: A Rust emulator for the MOS 6502 microprocessor.
longDescription: A complete emulation of the MOS Technology 6502 microprocessor written in Rust — the CPU behind the NES, Commodore 64, and Apple II. An exploration of instruction-set architecture, opcode decoding, and cycle-accurate timing.

name: RChip-8
description: A highly portable CHIP-8 emulator written in Rust.
longDescription: A CHIP-8 virtual machine and emulator built in Rust with portability as a first-class goal — designed to run across desktop and constrained targets. A study in interpreter design, opcode decoding, and display/timing emulation.

name: RemoteWindow
description: A window-sharing app that streams application windows over the network.
longDescription: A network-based window-sharing application in Rust for real-time sharing of application windows across machines. Research into remote-desktop protocols, network streaming, and efficient graphics transmission.

name: TunnelExperiment
description: A middleman server that forwards incoming TCP requests to a given server.
longDescription: An experimental TCP proxy that acts as a middleman, forwarding network requests to a target server. Research into network protocols, connection management, and proxy-server architectures.

name: LaserNet
description: Bi-directional laser communication research on microcontrollers — timing and packet loss.
longDescription: An experimental bi-directional laser communication system built with microcontrollers to study optical communication: timing synchronization, packet-loss analysis, and signal integrity in free-space optical links. An exploration of the challenges of reliable communication over laser.

name: Comparison of Pairing Functions: Szudzik, Cantor, and Bit Interleaving
description: A visual and mathematical comparison of Szudzik's, Cantor's, and bit-interleaving pairing functions, with an interactive chart and code.
longDescription: This experiment explores and visualizes three pairing functions (Szudzik, Cantor, bit interleaving) that uniquely map two integers into one. Includes an interactive chart and code for comparison.

name: Compressing Color: YUV, YIQ & Chroma Subsampling
description: An interactive look at how analog TV and modern video shrink an image by exploiting the eye’s weak color acuity.
longDescription: A live, in-browser demo of RGB → Y′CbCr / YIQ colour-space conversion and 4:2:2 / 4:2:0 chroma subsampling — separating luma from chroma, blurring the color, and measuring the byte savings and error (PSNR) in real time on a canvas.
